dimensions.assessment: Affects medical school graduates entering forensic fellowships, medicolegal death investigators, forensic toxicologists, and accredited publicly funded medical examiner and coroner offices.
dimensions.evidence: graduate medical education program... publicly funded medical examiner or coroner office... publicly funded forensic toxicology laboratory

dimensions.assessment: Provides targeted fellowships, training, salary support, and certification funding for specific professional fields.
dimensions.evidence: provide payment to individuals selected by such entity for a forensic pathology fellowship for salary, fringe benefits

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes appropriations of $13,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2028 through 2032, and makes fellowship payments non-taxable.
dimensions.evidence: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $13,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2028 through 2032.

dimensions.assessment: Amends the Public Health Service Act by adding a new subpart for a forensic pathology workforce grant program.
dimensions.evidence: Part E of title VII of the Public Health Service Act (42 U.S.C. 294n et seq.) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes grant funding over a five-year period from fiscal year 2028 through fiscal year 2032.
dimensions.evidence: for each of fiscal years 2028 through 2032

missing_information: The exact long-term economic impact beyond the authorized appropriation amounts.
importance_detail.rationale: Authorizes $13,000,000 annually from fiscal years 2028 through 2032 for grants to address shortages in the forensic pathology workforce, medical examiner offices, and toxicology laboratories.
